scores.evidence: Resending is safe because Yjs updates are idempotent.
scores.rationale: Yjs, y-protocols sync, relative positions, UndoManager and append-only log are used correctly; minor issues such as 'offline comes for free', 'AP with strong eventual consistency' alongside a per-doc single owner, and server-side validation of opaque CRDT updates (hard to do) without discussing it.

scores.evidence: plain text in a `<textarea>` bound to a `Y.Text`, with no rich text, cursors or styling.
scores.rationale: Covers collaboration, offline, history, presence, comments, sharing with explicit deferrals and reasons; some feasibility leaps (server-side validation of Yjs updates, 24h offline merges) remain.

scores.evidence: The server still relays, stores and authorizes.
scores.rationale: Consistent split of api/collab, Postgres log, single-owner routing; minor tension: AP claim vs single owner, and 'no cross-node fan-out' vs horizontal scale handled via deferred trigger.

scores.evidence: 10k fuzz sessions with zero divergence. A `kill -9` on the collab node mid-edit loses zero acked updates.
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, early, with fuzz harness, chaos tests, divergence detector in prod, and nightly load tests; some thresholds are invented but revisit triggers are explicit.

scores.evidence: Switch to OT ... if more than 50 MB in memory for a large doc after compaction
scores.rationale: Revisit triggers show sensitivity, but scale, team size, compliance and budget assumptions are never stated and many numbers (200 editors, 500 GB, 20%) are unsupported thresholds.

scores.evidence: If a user lost access while offline, their rejected edits are saved as a private copy, never dropped silently.
scores.rationale: Covers divergence, crash loss, duplicates, revocation while offline, memory DoS, XSS paste, bad snapshot, auth provider outage, DLQ, with detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: One-command rollback to the previous image.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, drain, PITR, dashboards, alerts, SLO burn rates are concrete; incident ownership/on-call and operational burden for a small team are not addressed.

scores.evidence: Use WebRTC peer-to-peer for presence only, if server egress cost for presence dominates.
scores.rationale: Cost is mentioned only in passing in triggers; no build or run cost estimate, no scaling of cost with usage, Postgres log growth cost barely considered.

scores.evidence: Concurrency algorithm (most irreversible: it fixes the stored data format).
scores.rationale: Explicitly identifies irreversible decisions (algorithm, data format, schema, ACL granularity), freezes format early with version byte, add-only schema, revisit triggers and migration gating.

scores.evidence: Modular monolith: one repo, one codebase, two process types.
scores.rationale: Starts simple with textarea slice and monolith, defers multi-region and fan-out; some ceremony (transactional outbox, k6 nightly, OTel from day one) is slightly heavy but mostly justified.

scores.evidence: Exit check: In prod, two browsers converge on the same text, a reload restores it
scores.rationale: Walking-skeleton first slice, dependency-justified phases, concrete tasks and exit checks per phase, and revisit triggers; a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: CRDT using Yjs. Merges are commutative and idempotent ... Switch to OT (ShareDB-style, server-ordered) if CRDT tombstone or memory overhead goes over budget
A versioned ProseMirror/TipTap schema, add-only: node and mark types are never removed or renamed.
N simulated clients make random concurrent edits under partition, reordering and duplication. The test asserts that all replicas are identical
Each update is appended to the Postgres update log before the ack ... Never delete log entries until the snapshot is verified.
One process owns each doc, assigned by consistent hash on doc ID ... Client reconnect with exponential backoff and jitter.
The client keeps unacked updates in IndexedDB and resends them on reconnect.
when an ACL changes, the server closes or downgrades active sockets within 5 seconds.
A restore is applied as a *new forward update*; the log is never rewritten. ... Per-user undo with `Y.UndoManager`, tracking local edits only.
Awareness channel on the same socket. It is ephemeral (never persisted) ... Remote cursors and selections via relative positions.
Rich text depends on proven sync, so it waits.
Max update size of 1 MB to prevent memory DoS ... load tests on hot docs and large docs.
Clients below the minimum schema version are forced to reload.

traps.evidence: CRDT using Yjs ... the library is mature.
Rich text depends on proven sync, so it waits.
The server acks only after a durable write.
The server still relays, stores and authorizes.

note: Strong, sync-first, well-validated plan with good reversibility reasoning; weak on cost, explicit assumptions, and some depth on large-document limits and protocol versioning.
